text:
maya: FYI noticing a large spike in console chart render times since last canary rolled at ~2045676000. Dashboards dragging, LCP up ~600ms for heavy orgs :grimace:
alex: saw that too. Is it everywhere or only specific routes?
maya: mostly /metrics and /heatmap routes. Small orgs fine. Large orgs with many series hit a big slow down.
trent: throwing traces now. early suspicion: KV cache miss rate jumped after the routing change — keys look different when routed through policy-v2.
sahil: can you paste the trace id? I want to check batching and prefix cache behavior.
maya: trace: 9f4a2b3c. stack snippet from frontend:```
fetch('/api/console/query', {body: JSON.stringify(qs), headers:{'x-routing':'policy-v2'}})
.then(res => res.json())
.then(renderHeatmap)
.catch(e => console.warn(e))
```
alex: interesting — policy-v2 adds the region shard header which changed cache keys server-side. backend saw cache misses -> more full-query latency -> charts block while waiting for data.
perf-bot: perf-alert: chart-render-time P95 increased to 2.4s for /heatmap in prod since 2045676000.
maya: confirmed KV cache hit% dropped from 92% -> 48% on the metric-query cache.
trent: that's likely the root cause. Options: 1) revert routing header change 2) normalize cache key server-side to ignore routing header 3) add client-side per-route fallback skeletons and optimistic render to avoid blocking UI.
sahil: normalizing keys is safest long-term. But that needs backend deploy and QA. Revert would be fastest mitigation for customer-impact.
alex: re: bundle size — I did a quick check, we also pulled in a telemetry helper in the same release but its size is tiny. I don't think it's the bundle, it's the data pipeline.
maya: +1 on revert for immediate relief. Can someone trigger canary rollback for that deploy? deploy-bot: rollback started for canary group: console-canary-3 at 2045679123.
trent: I'll open a backend PR to normalize keys (strip routing header) and add tests for cache-key invariance. Draft: https://git.redwood/PR/4021
sahil: also let's add an observability metric: cache_key_variants_count per endpoint so we can detect key churn.
alex: UX idea: show a streaming skeleton for heatmap tiles so charts don't block entire panel while a large query completes. Low effort and reduces perceived slowness.
maya: agreed, but that's a bandaid. Prioritize rollback + backend key fix. UX can be follow-up.
perf-bot: rollback completed for canary at 2045679189. Canaries show 30% improvement in P95 in the first 5 minutes.
maya: Can everyone confirm if large-org dashboards are back to baseline?
trent: my traces look much better now — KV cache hit back to ~90% on sample traces.
sahil: leaving a follow-up ticket: CONSOLE-847 normalize cache keys + add invariant tests + telemetry metric.
alex: I'll prototype the skeleton streaming approach in a small PR, tag you all.
maya: thanks. Action items: rollback confirmed, backend PR 4021, ticket CONSOLE-847, UX PR queued. Closing thread once PRs are green. :tada:
